note: Short self-ratings about whole families of traits (the 10 scorecard categories and a general learner factor). Written by hand on 3 Nov 2026 and blind-judged the same day by two free models of different families (scripts/judge-factor-items.js, curriculum-build/onboarding-sim/factor-judge.json): two items were rewritten after the first runs (representation b pointed the opposite way to representation a; intake b read as attention, a pacing trait). Each pair: high = high on the factor, low = low. Read by services/onboarding/pool.js fq:* items.

g.high: New subjects usually click for me faster than they do for the people around me
g.low: New subjects usually take me longer to click than the people around me

g.high: I can usually learn something new from one good explanation
g.low: I usually need an explanation several times before I really get it

intake.high: I take in new information easily, whether I read it or hear it
intake.low: I find it hard to take in new information in one go

intake.high: I can keep several new facts in mind at once while I read or listen
intake.low: When several new facts come at once, some of them slip away from me

reasoning.high: I can usually see the rule or pattern behind a problem
reasoning.low: The rule or pattern behind a problem is usually hard for me to see

reasoning.high: I can follow an argument with several steps without losing the thread
reasoning.low: I lose the thread when an argument has several steps

pacing.high: I keep a steady working pace and settle into study quickly
pacing.low: My pace is uneven and it takes me a while to settle into study

pacing.high: I can switch back into my work easily after an interruption
pacing.low: After an interruption it is hard to get back into my work

engagement.high: I need my learning to be varied, lively and clearly useful to stay with it
engagement.low: I am fine with plain, steady material even when it is not varied or lively

engagement.high: Stories, humour and challenges make a big difference to how much I take in
engagement.low: Stories, humour and challenges make little difference to how much I take in

memory.high: What I learn stays with me for a long time
memory.low: What I learn fades quickly unless I go back over it

memory.high: I can usually recall things from memory without any prompt
memory.low: I usually need a prompt or a choice of answers to remember things

resilience.high: When I get something wrong I recover quickly and try again
resilience.low: When I get something wrong it knocks me and I find it hard to try again

resilience.high: I stay calm with hard problems and work through them before asking for help
resilience.low: Hard problems frustrate me and I want help straight away

metacognition.high: I check my own understanding and change how I study when it is not working
metacognition.low: I rarely check my own understanding or change how I study

metacognition.high: I plan my study and keep to the plan
metacognition.low: I rarely plan my study and mostly go as I feel

representation.high: I like clear steps, worked examples and detailed feedback
representation.low: I like to work things out from the problem with little guidance

representation.high: I learn best when each idea is shown more than one way, with every step written out
representation.low: One compact explanation is enough for me; I do not need every step shown

motivation.high: I study because I want to understand, even when no one is checking
motivation.low: I mostly study because of marks, rewards or other people's expectations

motivation.high: I keep going with a subject even when it is dull or hard
motivation.low: I lose interest in a subject once it is dull or hard

transfer.high: I often use ideas from one subject in another, or in daily life
transfer.low: I usually keep what I learn in one subject separate from the others

transfer.high: I like to understand the big idea and then apply it to new cases
transfer.low: I like to learn one case at a time and stay with the cases I was shown
